title: Publish record updates with fresh basis and coherent durable outcomes
statement: The system shall publish structurally valid explicit record replacements as one coherent durable transaction after checking expected revision, target identities, and declared decision-basis identities under writer exclusion, with contained writes, safe stale retries, and no usable mixed state.

what.problem: Competing writers, stale decisions, or partial publication can lose work or leave a reader with a combination of states that never existed coherently.
what.desired_outcome: A successful save identifies fully committed requested bytes; conflict, contention, and interruption remain explicit without overwriting an observed incompatible state.

why.rationale: Reliable mechanical publication is necessary even when the stored engineering judgment is incomplete, adverse, or awaiting review.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: During initial creation, targeted or advanced record publication, batch publication, repeated submissions, and concurrent supported reads/writes.

contexts: The exact allowed write set of one selected change, declared contained decision-basis subjects, and private transaction state.

how.approach: Use the same validation, containment, identity, writer-exclusion, and recoverable publication protections across every supported writer. Check revision before no-op recognition, prepare recovery before authoritative replacement, and report saved only after durable commitment with the required observed read-set checks.

how_much.scope: Preserves the published local save-safety boundary. CLI writers coordinate; outside edits are protected at observed identity checks only. An exact-target outside edit after the final check can be overwritten; no atomic exclusion of all external writers, platform expansion, or disaster-recovery service is promised.

acceptance_criteria: Every write names its expected revision, target set and identities, and declared decision-basis identities. Observed mismatches produce conflict requiring reread and a new actor decision, with no silent refresh or merge.

Competing CLI writers cannot overwrite one another. Supported readers obtain coherent before/after records or busy/recovery-required, never a usable mixed snapshot; saved means all requested replacement bytes are durably committed.

Primary, advanced, helper, creation, and recovery paths share path containment and protection against observed ancestor substitution. Cross-change writes, traversal, symlink escape, hard-linked authoritative targets, unsupported paths, and unexpected overwrite are rejected.

A fresh identical candidate returns unchanged only after current preconditions pass. A lost-response retry with the old revision conflicts even if the earlier save succeeded; no retry duplicates entries, increments semantic state, or creates new approval.

Observed decision-basis drift is checked before publication and again before commitment is reported. Drift after replacement triggers safe restoration or recovery-required, retaining the documented external-edit timing limitation.

All-or-none batch publication validates the complete final candidate and creates recovery information before replacement. Incomplete publication is explicitly recoverable and unavailable as coherent current state.
